title: POC scoping - Integration planning with NovusCommerce
summary: AE+SE run through POC success criteria, workload sizing and benchmark plan; agreement on testing OpenAI-compatible endpoints and function calling; discuss VPC/private deployment needs; next steps to run 2-week pilot benchmark with staging keys, share security docs and pricing.
transcript:
[00:00] Elena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - we wanted to scope the POC and make sure success criteria and integration steps are clear.
[00:07] Raj Patel: Thanks Elena, excited to get going. Quick context, we run realtime product recommendations on web + mobile, about 1200 reqs/sec peak across regions, typical session is 300 tokens average, sometimes up to 1k tokens for complex carts.
[00:22] Marcus Liu: Got it. So for the POC are you focused on generation (recommendation text) or embeddings and reranking?
[00:28] Sofia Martinez: Primary is generation for personalized snippets and followups, secondary is embeddings for similarity searches. We also want to validate structured output for downstream parsing into our commerce schema.
[00:39] Priya Rao: And in terms of infra, do you want hosted vs dedicated vs private?
[00:43] Daniel Cho: Security is a big one - we need VPC peering or private deployment; SOC2 docs; and KMS for keys. We can do hosted if traffic is isolated but prefer a private option for the pilot if feasible.
[00:55] Elena Park: Understood. For a POC we usually do a 2-week benchmark in a staging environment - we can provide OpenAI-compatible endpoints and SDKs so your engineers can swap in easily. We'll also run a Redwood Dedicated profile if you want to test reserved capacity and latency SLOs.
[01:10] Raj Patel: Timeline wise 2 weeks sounds good. Success criteria, we want median token latency under 200ms and 99th percentile under 800ms, throughput to sustain 500 rps for the pilot, and quality parity with our current model (human eval + basic BLEU-ish tests).
[01:23] Marcus Liu: Perfect. For workload sizing can you confirm average tokens per call and concurrency during the pilot?
[01:28] Sofia Martinez: Average 300 tokens, 95th perc ~700 tokens. For pilot we'll run synthetic burst patterns to simulate black friday-ish traffic - target 500 rps sustained with peaks to 900.
[01:39] Marcus Liu: Ok thanks. We'll size batch configs, KV cache warmup, and suggest quantization profile if you want lower cost. We recommend starting with our OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint and function calling enabled for structured JSON outputs.
[01:52] Daniel Cho: Quick question - function calling, can we map directly to our internal tool calls? We need strict schema enforcement so bad JSONs don't break downstream parsers.
[02:00] Priya Rao: Yes - Redwood supports structured output and a function-calling layer; SE note: schema enforcement is done client-side but we can add post-parse validation hooks and a fallback to a safe schema variant.
[02:12] Raj Patel: Also SDKs - we currently use Python/Node in prod. How are your SDKs?
[02:16] Elena Park: We have official Node and Python SDKs that are OpenAI-compatible; engineers typically swap the baseURL and API key and tests run. We also provide a lightweight Java SDK and REST examples. For the POC we'll share a sample repo with integration tests and a load harness.
[02:31] Sofia Martinez: For benchmarks, what metrics will you provide? We need latency histograms, token-level cost, per-route dashboards, and error traces.
[02:38] Marcus Liu: We'll provide token-level cost breakdowns, per-model latency, per-region breakdown, and KV cache hit rates. We'll also share A/B eval harness results.
[02:48] Daniel Cho: Data residency - do you store any customer data? Audit logs?
[02:52] Elena Park: We don't persist user input in hosted mode beyond short-term logs used for telemetry; for Dedicated/Private you control persistence. We'll share our SOC2 and an architecture diagram for VPC/private flows.
[03:04] Raj Patel: Ok. For benchmarks, let's define the test plan: week 1 - integration + smoke tests; week 2 - load and quality evals with human reviews. At the end we should have a report with P50/P95/P99, throughput curves, and cost per 1k tokens.
[03:19] Marcus Liu: Sounds good. I'll propose a concrete runbook: Day 0 - keys & repo; Day 1-2 - integration and sample validation (function call schemas); Day 3-5 - baseline runs; Day 6-10 - ramp to target throughput and stress tests; Day 11-12 - quality evals and human labeling; Day 13 - final report.
[03:36] Sofia Martinez: For function calling we need deterministic output - like we want the model to return a JSON with fields {product_id, score, reason, upsell_flag} and avoid free text. How strict is the enforcement?
[03:46] Priya Rao: You can pass a JSON schema and enable function calling; Redwood will surface parse errors and we can pipe responses through a schema validator. We also recommend a simple canonicalizer step in your pipeline.
[03:56] Daniel Cho: About cost - can you give rough pricing for the pilot (2 weeks) for 500 rps avg?
[04:01] Elena Park: We'll send a tailored estimate after we size exact token volumes; for a ballpark we'll put together a pricing note. Committed Dedicated vs hosted makes a big difference. We'll include spot numbers for quantized models.
[04:13] Raj Patel: Dev experience - we use GitHub Actions to deploy. Can the SDK be used in CI for integration tests and run the load harness?
[04:20] Marcus Liu: Yes the SDK CLI + sample dashboard can be integrated into CI. We'll include a GH Actions example that runs smoke tests against staging endpoint and fails CI on schema regression.
[04:30] Ava Green: Stakeholders: me (PM), Raj (CTO), Sofia (ML lead), Daniel (platform), plus legal/security for final signoff. Expect legal to ask about data processing and contract terms.
[04:40] Elena Park: We'll attach our security pack and a template SLA. For private deployment we'll outline options and timelines - private deployments can take 4-8 weeks depending on approvals, but for POC we can use VPC peering or dedicated pools to accelerate.
[04:55] Raj Patel: Any competitor concerns? We evaluated MegaCloud AI and also considered building in-house; main tradeoff is time-to-market vs control.
[05:03] Marcus Liu: Noted. We'll highlight latency and cost differences in the report.
[05:08] Priya Rao: Ok, let's recap next steps...
[05:10] Elena Park: Recap: 1) Redwood to share integration repo, security pack, and pricing estimate by EOD Friday. 2) Novus to provision staging infra and provide sample traffic profile and two test datasets (short and long prompts). 3) Schedule kickoff for Day 0 (keys & repo) next Monday. 4) Plan two-week benchmark run.
[05:26] Raj Patel: Sounds good, thank you.
[05:28] Marcus Liu: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the repo link.
[05:31] (call ends)
